record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.original_question: Can one construct new pairs of line arrangements B:g=0 and B':g'=0 in P^2 whose intersection lattices are isomorphic to each other but not equal to the lattice of the classical Ziegler example discussed earlier in the paper, and for which the minimal degrees mdr(g) and mdr(g') of nontrivial Jacobian relations are different?

evidence.quote: There is an interesting question to find new pairs of line arrangements, say B : g = 0 and B′ : g′ = 0 such that their intersection lattices verify L(B) = L(B′) 6= L(A) and mdr(g) 6= mdr(g′).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$. For a reduced homogeneous polynomial $g \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ defining a line arrangement $B: g=0$, let $J_g = (g_x, g_y, g_z)$ be the Jacobian ideal, and let
$$\mathrm{AR}(g) = \{(a,b,c) \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]^3 : a\, g_x + b\, g_y + c\, g_z = 0\}$$
be the graded module of Jacobian syzygies (relations among the partial derivatives). Define the minimal degree of a nontrivial Jacobian relation,
$$\mathrm{mdr}(g) = \min\{r \geq 0 : \mathrm{AR}(g)_r \neq 0\},$$
where one ignores the trivial Koszul-type relations (equivalently, $\mathrm{mdr}(g)$ is the smallest degree of a generator of the syzygy module of $J_g$). For a line arrangement $B$, let $L(B)$ denote its intersection lattice, i.e., the poset of nonempty intersections of subfamilies of lines, ordered by reverse inclusion. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote Ziegler's classical pair of two arrangements of nine lines sharing the same intersection lattice but having distinct $\mathrm{mdr}$; write $L(\mathcal{A})$ for the underlying intersection lattice.

Construct, or determine the existence of, a pair of line arrangements $B: g = 0$ and $B': g' = 0$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $L(B) \cong L(B')$ (the two arrangements have isomorphic intersection lattices),
\item $L(B) \not\cong L(\mathcal{A})$ (the common lattice is different from that of Ziegler's classical example),
\item $\mathrm{mdr}(g) \neq \mathrm{mdr}(g')$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has constructed new Ziegler pairs of line arrangements in the complex projective plane having the same underlying intersection lattice (matroid) but different free resolutions of the Milnor algebra, hence different mdr, beyond Ziegler's classical example. In particular, a 2024 preprint on the numerical Terao conjecture and Ziegler pairs exhibits a pair of arrangements of 13 lines with the same matroid and different mdr, and subsequent work (2025) provides general constructions of families of such pairs. Thus the question of producing new same-lattice/different-mdr examples appears to be affirmatively answered.

status_evidence.title: On the numerical Terao's conjecture and Ziegler pairs for line arrangements
status_evidence.snippet: We use the newly discovered singular matroid realization spaces to construct new examples of pairs of line arrangements having the same underlying matroid but different free resolutions of the Milnor algebras.
status_evidence.claim: New Ziegler-type pairs (same matroid, different algebraic invariants including mdr) beyond the classical Ziegler example have been constructed.

status_evidence.title: Addition theorems for Ziegler pairs of hyperplane arrangements
status_evidence.snippet: General construction yielding the first known families of Ziegler pairs in arbitrary dimension and size, starting from examples in the projective plane.
status_evidence.claim: Families of Ziegler pairs (same combinatorics, different derivation modules) are now constructed systematically.
